date_note: CyberScoop says the Justice Department announced the extradition on Monday 23 November; the page gives no extradition date.
title: Kosovo man Hektor Avdyli, indicted over stolen credit card data sales, extradited to the US
org: US Department of Justice / FBI Milwaukee
summary: CyberScoop reports the Justice Department announced that Hektor Avdyli, 21, of Kosovo, was extradited to the US and is in Milwaukee awaiting trial. A Wisconsin grand jury returned an eight-count indictment in October 2025 for wire fraud, access device fraud and aggravated identity theft. According to authorities, a hard drive in his possession at arrest held 2.7 million payment card numbers.
plain: CyberScoop reports a 21-year-old Kosovo man accused of selling stolen credit card data has been brought to the US to face trial in Milwaukee.
exec: CyberScoop reports a Kosovo suspect indicted over stolen card data was extradited to the US.

evidence.quote: A hard drive in his possession at the time of his arrest had 2.7 million payment card numbers on it, according to authorities.
In October 2025, a federal grand jury in Wisconsin returned an eight-count indictment charging Hektor Avdyli, 21.

validation.note: CyberScoop and FOX 9 (Minneapolis) each report the extradition, the October 2025 Milwaukee indictment and a hard drive with payment card numbers (CyberScoop: 2.7 million; FOX 9: roughly 2.7 million); FOX 9 quotes First Assistant U.S. Attorney Brad Schimel and FBI Milwaukee. The Justice Department release itself was not read.
